bug_semantics: Bastillion's AuthFilter ran only for container-matched /manage/* and /admin/* paths, while LMVC's BaseKontroller dispatched a controller whenever the raw request URI contained the annotated controller path plus .ktrl. An unauthenticated request with an arbitrary leading segment, such as /anything/manage/viewUsers.ktrl, therefore missed AuthFilter but still dispatched the privileged controller. The same path-prefix mismatch exposed reads and state-changing manager operations, including user and managed-system creation.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable dispatcher expression originated in the first public LMVC source commit bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8. Bastillion commit 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77 then replaced Struts with loophole.mvc:lmvc:1.00.00 while retaining prefix-only AuthFilter mappings, making the mismatch exploitable in Bastillion. LMVC package rename bfbfd89449b2f7441466fcbe770da57fbfd930bb and Bastillion source import fbfd6639227ee8a8f858229191c1639490a2618c preserve the line and are not BICs.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8. Its commit object has author and committer Sean Kavanagh <sean.p.kavanagh6@gmail.com>, timestamp 2018-04-17T09:52:34Z, message exactly 'Initial commit', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity. The Claude Co-Authored-By trailer on the 2026 fix is not BIC evidence.
evidence: Mechanism and exploit: GitHub issue https://github.com/bastillion-io/Bastillion/issues/669 records the /manage/* and /admin/* AuthFilter mappings, the vulnerable BaseKontroller request.getRequestURI().contains(c.path() + '.ktrl') dispatch, unauthenticated 200 access through /anything/manage/viewUsers.ktrl, manager-account creation through /x/manage/saveUser.ktrl, and validation on v4.0.2-SNAPSHOT ff84821 with LMVC 2.0.0. Smallest BIC: the preserved public LMVC history at https://github.com/lizhonghao2/lmvc/commit/bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8 shows BaseKontroller.java added in bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8 with the exact vulnerable contains expression; its direct parent tree https://github.com/lizhonghao2/lmvc/tree/4524a69036b627ceca788bf5fdc7779121dd569c contains only LICENSE, directly proving absence. The subsequent https://github.com/lizhonghao2/lmvc/commit/bfbfd89449b2f7441466fcbe770da57fbfd930bb is only a package rename. In the assigned Bastillion clone, `git show 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77 -- pom.xml src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml` shows the Struts-to-LMVC 1.00.00 cutover and the protected-prefix mappings; `git grep -n -e lmvc -e '\.ktrl' -e BaseKontroller 6bdce45fd829c022d602e7ff4ae6fa2172cbb757 -- pom.xml src/main/java src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml` returns no match in its parent. `git log --all -S'request.getRequestURI().contains(c.path() + DispatcherServlet.CTR_EXT)' -- src/main/java/loophole/mvc/base/BaseKontroller.java` identifies fbfd6639227ee8a8f858229191c1639490a2618c as the later in-repository source import, and its patch adds the already-existing LMVC line plus gitlink 8f9faf9853014268392936e97d8782d9bc5b1e6b. Fix boundary: `git grep` on d759fb686a1a097b1b026e286fd9b20e5ba349c8^ (4a63f4d2f10bc7d02d65cfd2848c4b0d17d6b98c) finds the vulnerable expression at BaseKontroller.java:148; the same command on d759fb686a1a097b1b026e286fd9b20e5ba349c8 finds the replacement request.getServletPath().equals(...) at line 157. `git tag --contains 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77` starts at v3.00.00, while `git tag --contains d759fb686a1a097b1b026e286fd9b20e5ba349c8` returns v5.2.0; v5.1.0 does not contain the fix. Issue 669 and the maintainer identify v5.2.0 as the fixed release, consistent with the advisory's affected boundary Bastillion <=5.1.0. BIC-only marker check is reproducible from https://api.github.com/repos/lizhonghao2/lmvc/git/commits/bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8, which returns the human author/committer and message with no trailers.
reasoning: The root cause is the LMVC raw-URI substring dispatcher, whose first public write is bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8. Direct inspection proves its parent lacks all framework code. The 2018 Bastillion LMVC adoption is the application-level activation boundary, and the 2026 wholesale source import is a migration, so neither supersedes the smaller upstream first-writer. The direct fix changes the dispatcher to exact matching on the container-normalized servlet path and ships in v5.2.0. Because the BIC commit object is a 2018 human commit with no AI attribution or bot identity, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI; AI attribution on the later fix is excluded.
